questions.q: Why does Extended Events replace SQL Trace / Profiler in this lesson's explanation?
options: SQL Trace/Profiler is deprecated, and Extended Events achieves the same tracing goal with much lower overhead by only capturing the events and fields you actually ask for
Extended Events is a newer name for exactly the same feature with no behavioral difference
Profiler was removed because it required an internet connection
Extended Events only works on Azure SQL, never on-prem SQL Server
questions.explain: Profiler's default footprint is comparatively heavy and chatty; Extended Events only adds overhead for the specific events you select.

questions.q: What are the four pieces that make up an Extended Events session, per this lesson?
options: Event, Action, Predicate, and Target
Table, View, Index, and Trigger
Server, Database, Schema, and Login
Session, Connection, Request, and Query
questions.explain: Event is what you capture, action is extra context, predicate filters it, and target is where the captured data goes.

questions.q: In the New Session wizard screenshot for this lesson, what is being configured on the "Data Storage" page?
options: Where the session's captured data actually goes — an event file on disk for a durable capture, or in-memory only for a short live look
Which SQL Server edition is licensed for this server
The database's backup retention policy
The number of CPU cores allocated to the instance
questions.explain: Saving to a file lets you walk away and review results later; an in-memory-only target disappears when the session stops.

questions.q: What does sys.fn_xe_file_target_read_file do, and why is it useful?
options: It reads a session's .xel file directly and returns captured events as XML, so you can review results in plain T-SQL without the SSMS UI
It permanently deletes an Extended Events session
It creates a new SQL Server login for the watcher service
It is a DAX function used only in Power BI
questions.explain: This table-valued function lets you shred captured event XML for specific fields like duration or the statement text, entirely in T-SQL.

questions.q: What is a predicate, in the context of an Extended Events session?
options: A filter condition so the session only captures events matching it, e.g. only statements taking longer than 500ms
The name of the SQL Server instance being monitored
The physical disk location where SQL Server data files are stored
A synonym for the Target piece of the session
questions.explain: Predicates keep a session's captured data focused and its overhead low by excluding events that don't match the condition.
